messages.author: 62e4302182c06d02
messages.subject: is 'stringr' really supported ?
parts:
Per your package docs it looks like Renjin supports the "stringr" package, but I get the runtime exception below. It looks like the jvm is trying to find a native library, which contradicts your 100% java implementation. Please advise. Thanks.

Exception in thread "main" org.renjin.eval.EvalException: Could not find class for 'native' methods for package 'stringi' (className='org.renjin.cran.stringi.stringi')
at org.renjin.primitives.Native.getPackageClass(Native.java:324)
at org.renjin.primitives.Native.dotCall(Native.java:268)
at org.renjin.primitives.R$primitive$$Call.apply(R$primitive$$Call.java:60)

messages.author: 39ae60762c088189
messages.subject: Re: is 'stringr' really supported ?
parts:
Hi,

stringr indeed depends on stringi and also on magrittr. All three packages currently build for Renjin (stringi didn't at the time you tried), which means that their namespaces can be loaded in Renjin. However, if you look at these packages then you will see that most tests (i.e. examples) fail therefore they cannot be actually used at this moment. We are looking into improving the wording on http://packages.renjin.org to better reflect the state of packages in Renjin and we'll include your experience in designing a better user experience.

Regards,

Maarten-Jan

messages.subject: Re: is 'stringr' really supported ?

The version of stringi on packages.renjin.org is built from this fork of the package:

parts:
Sorry, it was the default branch on the forked repo, I've fixed that now.

The licensing shouldn't be a problem - Renjin's stringi fork can keep it's BSD license, which is the same as icu4j. 

Unfortunately, icu4j library doesn't seem to be an exact replacement for icu. Most disappointingly, it doesn't seem to include any sort of regular expression implementation, at least none that I could find in their javadoc:
http://icu-project.org/apiref/icu4j/  ...

-Alex

messages.subject: Re: is 'stringr' really supported ?
parts:
About regular expressions, I have been comparing documentation of both stringi-search and Java Pattern:
http://www.gagolewski.com/software/stringi/manual/?manpage=stringi-search-regex
https://docs.oracle.com/javase/7/docs/api/java/util/regex/Pattern.html

As they both refer to Unicode Regular Expressions (TR18), I would tend to believe they offer the same functionalities.

In parallel, I have been using the UnicodeSet from ICU in order to reimplement all the three stri_trim_* functions, as an exercise. I am however worried since the tests for stri_trim.Rd are still failing when run locally. I just opened a pull request for you to review.

Best regards,
Alain

messages.author: c486c05137a7f39b
messages.subject: Re: is 'stringr' really supported ?
parts:
Thanks again for pointing me to the right folder.

This way I already could more easily implement and fix the necessary code to pass locally the examples in stri_split.Rd for which I opened yet another pull request.

I know this "small pull requests" kind of progress has both advantages and disadvantages for you. But from my side, I feel like your team has more opportunities to stop me from committing undesired code and give me some more frequent feedback about your expectations.

On a long term perspective, I would like to reach the point where knitr would work with Renjin. But the first step would already be to reach a milestone where stringr would be usable.Would it be possible to somehow monitor the progress of this endeavor through the stringr build pages?
For example http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/stringr/1.2.0/build/15 show a global build failure while http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/stringr/1.2.0/build/14 presents a summary for each group of examples.
How often are these builds rerun? What triggers them?

Best regards,
Alain

PS: About the "new" build for stringi, I was surprised to read the version value in the dependency descriptor:
    <groupId>org.renjin.cran</groupId>
    <artifactId>stringi</artifactId>
    <version>0.2.15-renjin-1</version>

For example http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/stringr/1.2.0/build/15 show a global build failure while http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/stringr/1.2.0/build/14 presents a summary for each group of examples.
How often are these builds rerun? What triggers them?

The build pages you've linked to above are the results from building from the orginal package sources, and so are no longer relevant.

A word of explanation on our build system:

Nearly all of the packages on packages.renjin.org are built directly from the original package sources, so the reports are really focused on the results from simply unpacking the sources and building automatically for Renjin.

For the handful of packages like stringi where we've forked the package and written our own code to replace portions of the original package, we've carved out a special category in our database. These packages are flagged as "replaced" and handled specially.

These "replacement" packages are built by specific Jenkins jobs, which are generally triggered by a commit to our fork's GitHub repo and produce a new release with a version that's in the format "{package source base version}-renjin-bXX". I'm not sure what went wrong with the version number you highlighed below, I will double check the configuration.

http://build.renjin.org/job/Replacement-Packages/job/stringi/

Unfortunately, we haven't built out the system so far to produce the same kind of nice build reports that "normal" packages get, but the same results are available from the Jenkins job, for example, here is the output from the stri_trim.Rd file:

http://build.renjin.org/job/Replacement-Packages/job/stringi/org.renjin.cran$stringi/7/testReport/(root)/stri_trim-examples/_root_/

The stringi build job will push the new binary to our repo and register the build in the package database as *the* version for this package, and *all* "normal" packages that depend on stringi will use this version.

I've also set up the stringi job above to trigger builds for a few downstream packages of stringi, including stringr and knitr everytime you commit to stringi.

For example, you can see the results of stringr's tests based on your latest work on stringi:
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/stringr/1.2.0/build/16

HTH,

Hi Alain,
This was my mistake... I changed the signature of the DllSymbol class which broke binary compatibility with our stringi builds, so none of the methods you implemented were loaded or used.

The worst case was for knitr as you noticed, which uses stringi during it's "build" phase, so the problem led to the knitr build failing and becoming unavailable to other builds.

The package html page is set up to show the last build that succeeded, which meant that you were seeing results from earlier builds with earlier versions of stringi and Renjin.

The regression was flagged in our QA dashboard:
http://packages.renjin.org/qa/dashboard

And fixed in 0.8.2545. (so the regression may no longer be visible on the dashboard above).

Sorry for the inconvenience!

Alex
